universe: All filers · market cap ≥ $100M (USD-equivalent) · all 52 companies in Banks - Diversified · per-company metrics, market-cap-weighted · most recent fiscal year

metrics.label: EVA (Economic Value Added)
metrics.definition: Each company's EVA = NOPAT − (its own WACC) × Invested Capital, then market-cap-weighted across the sector. Dollar profit earned above the full cost of capital.

metrics.label: EVA Margin
metrics.definition: Each company's EVA ÷ Revenue, market-cap-weighted across the sector. Economic profit per dollar of sales.

metrics.label: ROIC
metrics.definition: Each company's NOPAT ÷ Invested Capital (Equity + Debt), market-cap-weighted. Return earned on capital employed.

metrics.label: WACC
metrics.definition: Each company's full WACC — CAPM cost of equity (the live 10-year Treasury yield plus beta times the live implied equity risk premium) blended with its after-tax cost of debt — market-cap-weighted. The hurdle ROIC must clear.

metrics.label: ROIC − WACC Spread
metrics.definition: ROIC minus WACC, market-cap-weighted across the group and derived from the weighted ROIC and weighted WACC so the three numbers reconcile. The core value-creation test. A positive spread means invested capital earns more than it costs, so growth builds value. A negative spread means returns sit below the cost of capital, so growth destroys it.

metrics.label: ROE
metrics.definition: Each company's Net Income ÷ Equity, market-cap-weighted. The return to shareholders — but on its own it is not a value-creation verdict (leverage inflates it); read it against the cost of equity below.

metrics.label: Cost of Equity (Ke)
metrics.definition: Each company's CAPM cost of equity (the live 10-year Treasury yield plus beta times the live implied equity risk premium), market-cap-weighted. The equity hurdle rate — the right benchmark for banks and insurers, where ROIC/WACC are undefined because debt is operating raw material.

metrics.label: Excess Return (ROE − Ke)
metrics.definition: Each company's ROE minus its cost of equity, market-cap-weighted (Damodaran, Ch.21). The direct equity value-creation test: positive = value created (P/B should exceed 1), negative = value destroyed. The equity-only twin of ROIC − WACC.

metrics.label: Justified P/B
metrics.definition: Each company's (ROE − g)/(Ke − g), market-cap-weighted — the price-to-book the fundamentals warrant. Compare with actual P/B: a low P/B is only cheap if it sits above the justified level.

metrics.label: Actual P/B
metrics.definition: Each company's Market Cap ÷ Book Equity, market-cap-weighted. For financials, book value tracks market value of net assets closely, so P/B (read against ROE − Ke) is the core relative-value lens.

metrics.label: P/E Ratio
metrics.definition: Each company's Market Cap ÷ Net Income (profitable companies only), market-cap-weighted across the group. The price investors pay for each dollar of current earnings. A higher group P/E reflects optimism or higher expected growth, so comparing P/E across sectors shows where the market is paying up for a story and where it is cautious.

metrics.label: Value Score
metrics.definition: The scorecard's 0-100 value score for this group, blending the scorecard measures with the most weight on economic profit (the ROIC minus WACC spread and EVA margin). A higher score means the group screens as a stronger value creator than its peers. It is a screening rank, not a valuation. Click the score to open the full method.

metrics.label: Net Interest Margin
metrics.definition: Net interest income (interest income − interest expense) ÷ total assets, market-cap-weighted across the spread-based LENDERS in the group only (interest income ≥ 20% of revenue). The core driver of bank profitability — the spread between what a bank earns on assets and pays on funding. A conservative proxy: true NIM uses average earning assets, which the dataset does not break out.

metrics.label: DuPont · Tax Burden (NI/EBT)
metrics.definition: Each company's Net Income ÷ Pre-tax Income (EBT), market-cap-weighted. Tax-retention lever of the 5-factor DuPont — the share of pre-tax profit that survives taxes.

metrics.label: DuPont · Interest Burden (EBT/EBIT)
metrics.definition: Each company's Pre-tax Income ÷ Operating Income (EBIT), market-cap-weighted. Interest-burden lever — the share of operating profit that survives interest and non-operating items.

metrics.label: DuPont · EBIT Margin (EBIT/Rev)
metrics.definition: Each company's Operating Income ÷ Revenue, market-cap-weighted. Operating-profitability lever. Tax × Interest × EBIT-margin = net margin.

metrics.label: DuPont · Net Profit Margin
metrics.definition: Each company's Net Income ÷ Revenue, market-cap-weighted. Profitability summary — equals Tax Burden × Interest Burden × EBIT Margin. Full 5-factor: ROE = Tax × Interest × EBIT-margin × Turnover × Multiplier.

metrics.label: DuPont · Asset Turnover
metrics.definition: Each company's Revenue ÷ Total Assets, market-cap-weighted. The efficiency lever.

metrics.label: DuPont · Equity Multiplier
metrics.definition: Each company's Total Assets ÷ Equity, market-cap-weighted. The leverage lever.

metrics.label: Operating Margin
metrics.definition: Each company's Operating Income ÷ Revenue, market-cap-weighted. Core profitability before financing and tax.

metrics.label: Net Margin
metrics.definition: Each company's Net Income ÷ Revenue, market-cap-weighted. Bottom-line profitability.

metrics.label: Revenue Growth
metrics.definition: Each company's year-over-year revenue growth, market-cap-weighted across the group. The aggregate top-line growth rate. Compare against the economy's own nominal growth (the Economic page carries the live GDP series).

metrics.label: Net Income Growth
metrics.definition: Each company's year-over-year net income growth, market-cap-weighted across the group. The aggregate bottom-line growth rate; it can swing far more than revenue because costs and one-off items move profit sharply.

metrics.label: Operating Leverage (DOL)
metrics.definition: Each company's %Δ Operating Income ÷ %Δ Revenue (latest two years), market-cap-weighted. Above 1 = profits amplify revenue swings.

metrics.label: Capex / Depreciation
metrics.definition: Each company's Capital Expenditure ÷ Depreciation & Amortization, market-cap-weighted. Above 1 = investing beyond maintenance.

metrics.label: Sales / Invested Capital
metrics.definition: Each company's Revenue ÷ Invested Capital, market-cap-weighted. Capital productivity.

metrics.label: FCF / Net Income
metrics.definition: Each company's Free Cash Flow ÷ Net Income (positive-earnings companies), market-cap-weighted. Earnings quality — how much profit converts to cash.

metrics.label: Net Debt / OCF
metrics.definition: Each company's Net Debt ÷ Operating Cash Flow (positive-OCF companies), market-cap-weighted. Years to repay net debt. Lower is safer.

metrics.label: Liabilities / Equity
metrics.definition: Each company's Total Liabilities ÷ Equity, market-cap-weighted. Total balance-sheet leverage.

metrics.label: P / Tangible Book
metrics.definition: Each company's price ÷ tangible book value, market-cap-weighted. Note: the current dataset's tangible book equals book value (intangibles are not subtracted), so this presently mirrors P/B.

metrics.label: Financial Leverage (Assets/Equity)
metrics.definition: Each company's Total Assets ÷ Equity, market-cap-weighted. The bank business-model proxy — spread lenders run 8-15x; it is the lever that turns thin NIMs into double-digit ROE.

metrics.label: Sustainable Growth g
metrics.definition: Each company's retention ratio × ROE, market-cap-weighted (Damodaran Ch.21). Given the regulatory focus on capital, retained earnings determine how fast a financial firm can expand.

metrics.label: Dividend Yield
metrics.definition: Each company's dividend yield, market-cap-weighted across the industry. The cash return to shareholders at current prices.

metrics.label: Payout Ratio
metrics.definition: Each company's dividends ÷ net income, market-cap-weighted. Above 100% = paying out more than it earns (unsustainable without balance-sheet support).
